# Exact recorded-node Core cleanup

Read docs/architecture/tailnet-node-cleanup.md. The existing owner controller and captured root daemon supply authority, not caller paths, names, peers, tags or an SDK string parameter. Require the original locked cloud/allocation/provider binding and settled provider deletion evidence before an API request. Preserve current deployment diagnosis, replacement, strict unique-key decoding and captured Self projection. Do not add agent or companion MCP provider-delete authority.

Process exact saved-tailnet bindings independently. Confirm only the exact saved-tailnet/device group after HTTP200/204, and save before the next request. Preflight confirmation must fit existing bounds. Never send an API request for an unresolved capture attempt, infer its device or mark it confirmed after another receipt succeeds. A known receipt can succeed while the untouched attempt still yields a manual outcome. Missing required, foreign or unsettled provider journals refuse dispatch; another original provider stays manual. Keep all404 uncertain.

Already-Deleted node cleanup retry reads original durable journals without new provider credentials or GETs. A Prepared cloud without enrollment evidence retains its existing provider storage-finalization retry. Missing/offline/denied/API or save uncertainty preserves IDs and fixed manual messages. None without enrollment evidence makes no API request. Preserve SDK OAuth classification/deadlines and private managed-slot/tombstone resolver. Keep confirmation flags, paired migration/version fences and nested duplicate-key refusal; older strict readers reject true confirmation. No record follows a successor automatically. Deleted-cloud redeploy must use the same locked require_complete check before public-key validation, storage-journal release or history reset. Exercise Delete→Redeploy with selected legacy missing identity, unknown attempts and unconfirmed receipts; refusal must preserve journals and original history. Confirmed receipts, genuinely never-provisioned state and None without enrollment remain allowed. Normal card removal and automatic close must recheck pending receipts and selected legacy missing-ID state under the original lifecycle lock, preserving the card and precise manual/API reason. Explicit native RemoveAnyway stays deliberate and locked, warns that retry controls disappear, and preserves the original resource record/ledger without API confirmation. Text matching preserves UI detail only, never authority. Actual first/final native/provider/API qualification cannot be claimed from synthetic tests.

This final outcome enables the backend through Core cloud-workspaces, preserving UI and owner CLI activation parity without a feature cycle. API dispatch and the shared can_remove pending-node check must stay enabled together. Native precise-reason/retry/card-retention and explicit-discard-warning behavior must accompany default activation.

Removal eligibility and recorded-node checks run on the existing background removal worker.
Display advice never authorizes discard: a fresh final check retains the original Store lock through exact-context UI application.
Cancellation, context drift and old generations cannot apply a later removal.
The UI preserves an earlier precise API failure only for the same displayed saved-tailnet/device pair; text supplies no authority.
A retained Ready connection watch does not prevent explicit RemoveAnyway, while busy operations and the lifecycle lock still refuse it.

For Docker deletion, preserve never-requested Prepared durably only with no port
intent and owned-container absence; volume-only preparation is not enrollment.
A container observed by any lookup must save Requested, including final
verification after earlier absence. Use the shared SDK observation path for both
SDK lookups; final verification must save before returning an error. Save failure forbids removal; lost replies/retries retain
uncertainty. Never infer freshness from a synthetic Terminated ID or erase legacy
readiness/stop/resume history. Exercise all three actual controller lookups, including a final-only observation
followed by container absence before retry.

Cleanup Retry settings reads must stay off the UI thread. Install the busy receiver before dispatch and check cancellation after a delayed read. Failed preflight must not invoke provider or node cleanup. Preserve the existing failed-preflight watch behavior for live workers.

Keep one display-only cleanup_retry context for recorded pending cleanup or legacy missing identity. A failure alone must not clear it. Settings failure, cancellation, invalid launch identity and lifecycle lock contention must retain Deleted, the error and Retry through normal event polling. A second delayed Retry must stay asynchronous. Preserve the legacy manual missing-ID explanation beside a later generic error. An empty Deleted snapshot does not settle legacy cleanup. A fresh Deleted snapshot with pending recorded receipts must replace Legacy display context with Recorded, remove the obsolete legacy explanation and keep Retry.

Clear obsolete context on authoritative non-Deleted Stage, Ready, successful Deleted completion, Stopped, Resumed or a snapshot with a non-Deleted stage or fully confirmed recorded ledger. Neither this context nor a cached snapshot authorizes Delete or removal. Recheck the original locked Store and current durable evidence for every node request, normal removal and redeploy. Exercise failure retention for recorded and legacy cases, snapshot/event reset and refusal to remove an unresolved Store record after display context clears.

Establish legacy display context on the first ordinary Remove failure, before a second busy Remove can replace the missing-ID error. Emit the exact saved Deleted snapshot under the original Store before cleanup and emit the last durable ledger after cleanup succeeds or fails. A failed save must publish no invented fact. Exercise first Ready deletion with a contended UI reload and both pending-failure and fully confirmed completion; the former retains Retry and the latter clears it without a reload. Do not infer Deleted stage from error text.

For restored legacy cards, inspect the raw record reason for warning presentation. A rendered STATE_UNKNOWN prefix must not hide the warning. Display text still supplies no removal authority.
